correctness.rationale: Circle minimizers occur at reports by the slope-jump argument; a four-report optimal point forces at most two reports in either side-plus-antipode count, permitting normal form (-a,0,b,c), 0<=a<=1/2,0<=b<=c<=1/2. Four exact facility costs and published EPCD gap probabilities yield F=5OPT-4EPCD with three rigorously nonnegative polynomial forms; equality classification isolates (1/4,0,1/4). RD<=3OPT/2 by pairwise triangle summation and the same profile realizes equality for both bounds. Thus all lambda mixtures have exact sharp (5+lambda)/4, including duplicates and boundary gaps. Symbolic algebra confirmed all three polynomial identities; standalone exact-rational program tested 37,136 profiles plus 4,851 case-identity inputs. Finite checks are ancillary, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The four-agent case is the first even nontrivial population to which the published deletion-extension mechanism applies. It has a genuine finite-population improvement over the known 3/2 population-uniform factor: MRP is exactly 11/8 and EPCD alone 5/4. The result also gives the entire fixed mixture efficiency frontier and a unique extremal geometry for all lambda<1, showing that equal mixing, asymptotically motivated for all populations, is not optimal within this mechanism family at n=4. This is a complete natural base-case phase law, not a parameter substitution or grid-only datum.
